gpu: 8 x NVIDIA L20X, SM90, 132 SM/GPU; single-node EP8
scope: Analyze restored production once-per-block row-to-column conversion. Do not continue repeated conversion inside dW GEMM. Diagnostic source edits restored; no performance implementation change.
numerics: E4M3, actual-column amax with pow2 scales, FP32 accumulation and BF16 dW; existing FP8 AB/Z cache boundaries unchanged.

methods.production: CUPTI production main kernels, 8 priming + 3 warmups + 5 measured samples, per-iteration slowest-rank duration then median. Nominal tokens8192/20480, variable per-rank tokens std0.1 and routing bias0.5; identical FP8/BF16 input hashes. Weight preparation excluded.
methods.timeline: Separate diagnostic native and adapter. Extra BWD events, retain timeline context/handle. Last measured sample per shape saved on all eight ranks, zero overflow. FWD preparation is outside backward-only timing. Task sums are CTA service, not wall time or hardware utilization; task granularity differs between BF16/FP8. Rowcol is nested in dH and is not additive to dH.
methods.native_status: Five sample task-service sums and phase durations. Compute all differences inside the same rank GPU clock domain. Heavy rank selected per sample by longest dgrad duration. Cross-rank globaltimer epochs are not comparable.
methods.ncu: Production Qwen35B EP8 rank2, 20480 fixed tokens/rank, route bias0.5; each counter group run separately, no cache flush or clock manipulation. Only successful single-pass reports accepted. These durations are not substituted for unprofiled benchmarks.
methods.dw_tail: For each CTA trace begin/end around assigned dW work, excluding final combine/rank join. Work interval fill=sum CTA intervals/(num CTA * dW interval span). This includes waits and is not hardware utilization. Last-quarter tail=(last end - 75th percentile end)/span. Single sample, requires repeated unprofiled A/B for optimization claims.

findings.evidence: About13us FP8 vs5-6us BF16 per tile after S-slot reuse wait. Existing path quantizes cached A/B, decodes them to preserve the forward/backward recomputation boundary, applies SwiGLU and casts H.
findings.candidate: Reduce conversion/reduction/layout-store instruction cost and live ranges while preserving AB/Z numerical boundaries. SASS confirms dynamic subgroup-mask MATCH.ANY/collective fallback code. Try uniform-mask width4 shuffles/reductions on full tiles with correct tail handling; keep packed conversion numerical behavior.
findings.status: Measured cost; optimization speedup not tested.

findings.topic: BWD SwiGLU and once-per-block column casts
findings.evidence: FP8 SwiGLU+quant service roughly33-35% of dgrad task service, per routed row2.1-2.7xBF16. Separately, X/dY row-col exposed region ~11-21% of dgrad task service and is a subset of dH. It includes X async-copy wait and math synchronization.
findings.candidate: Optimize packed conversion, actual-amax reduction, warp/column ownership and shared scratch/live ranges. Keep one conversion globally reused. Do not infer that moving it into every GEMM removes the same cost.
findings.status: Measured intervals; rowcol pure arithmetic vs copy-wait not separately attributed.

findings.evidence: Production20K dW exposed after combine~1.35/4.96/8.68ms forQ35/Q122/Flash. Diagnostic slowest dW rank Q35 lastquarterCTA tail~35%, work intervalfill~71%; Flashfill~99.5%, lastquartertail~0.3%.
findings.candidate: For coarse-tail cases examine long-expert work ordering and finer terminal task claims first; splittingK adds reduction/workspace and changes reduction order. ForFlash prioritize WGMMA/FP32 scale-promotion loop, not scheduler-tail fixes. Generic early-dW and pipelined-promotion attempts already lack demonstrated benefit.
findings.status: Diagnostic single-sample tail is a hypothesis guide, not a speedup prediction.

findings.evidence: Q35 FP8 firstoperand median~23-25us vs~1us forothermodels. At20K BF16Q35 is~32us too. Matched same-CTA same-tile intervals show93% of FP8 first-stage wait overlaps producer x_full publication wait (8K/20K). This is mostly waiting for pulled X to be published, not isolated TMA transfer latency.
findings.candidate: Inspect row-at-a-time peer pull, metadata/fence/publication overhead and ring-reuse credits. Batch/prefetch rows or change pull scheduling only after separating these causes. Source quantization already completed before main launch; do not attribute this wait to quantization inside GEMM.
findings.status: Producer publication overlap measured; pull subcauses not fully attributed.

findings.evidence: Mostloaded rank joins in~4-6us while light ranks waitmilliseconds. dgrad vs routedrows correlation>.99, maxload/mean~1.30-1.35. SourceX/dY quant20K~77-147us each; no notify overlap. Padding~1-2% at20K.
findings.candidate: Deprioritize barrier removal and source-quant hiding relative to conversion/service costs. Cross-rank work balance requires placement/routing-level changes, not deleting a necessary synchronization.
findings.status: No communication bandwidth bottleneck established from rank-join spans.

limitations: No end-to-end speedup claim: this turn profiles and analyzes the fixed224 implementation.
Whole-kernel Tensor-active percentage is not directly comparable as compute efficiency across BF16/FP8 peaks; combined with other counters and phase timing it motivates further analysis.
The grouped stall collection requires multiple replay passes and is rejected; do not use it to attribute precise stall percentages.
Diagnostic timing perturbs scheduling; final optimization acceptance must use same-workload unprofiled A/B and correctness checks.
reproduction: Use a clean checkout of base_commit; apply benchmarks/experiments/fp8_profile_review/baseline.patch (fixed224/56).
mkdir -p build/fp8-profile-review; copy the experiment scripts and patches there.
python build/fp8-profile-review/complete_trace.py (temporarily instruments and restores production source)
python build/fp8-profile-review/ncu.py (bounded EP8 capture; accepts one-pass only)

sass.finding: Dynamic four-lane mask collectives generate MATCH.ANY, conditional BRA.DIV, and WARPSYNC.COLLECTIVE fallback blocks. ExamplePC0xdd50 branches to0x24370 wrappingREDUX.MAX withWARPSYNC/ENDCOLLECTIVE. Extra static instructions and paths are confirmed; dynamic cost has not been attributed by instruction counters.
sass.candidate: For complete tiles, all lanes can participate with a uniform full-warp mask; use width4 shuffles and two xor/max rounds for4-lane amax. Tail rows require predication/neutral values or a correct fallback. Preserve NaN behavior and all existing AB/Z rounding. Keep register budgets224/56.
